docs.title: Welcome to CTF Arena
docs.text: CTF Arena is a self-hosted, lightweight Capture The Flag (CTF) platform built using Flask, SQLAlchemy, and Tailwind CSS templates. It is designed to host college and community-level cybersecurity events with native Docker-based challenge environments.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• 🏠 Challenge Grid: Dynamic catalog filtering by category, search, or difficulty.
  • 📡 Live Scoreboard: Real-time scoreboard streams powered by Server-Sent Events (SSE).
  • ⏱️ Dynamic Decay: Points scale dynamically based on solve counts or competition time elapsed.
  • 🔑 Built-in RBAC: Admin, Moderator, Challenge Author, and Participant privilege separation.
  • 🐳 Docker Exploits Sandbox: Competitors provision their own isolated containers in a sandbox.
  • 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Team Mode: Form teams to combine scores on the leaderboard.
  • 📊 Metrics & Observability: Native Prometheus /metrics and detailed /health endpoints.

docs.title: Administration & CLI Guide
docs.text: Manage competition settings, reset scores, export standings, and perform maintenance using the Admin UI or the Flask CLI.

docs.title: 1. CLI Commands
docs.text:
Run commands from the virtual environment:

# Database Setup
flask db upgrade

# Seeding Initial Defaults
flask seed

# Reset all competitor scoreboards (DANGEROUS)
flask reset-scores

# Background task prune containers
flask prune-instances

docs.title: 2. Platform Monitoring
docs.text:
Check /health or scrape /metrics using Prometheus:

# prometheus.yml config snippet
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'ctf-arena'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['localhost:5000']

docs.title: REST API Reference
docs.text: CTF Arena exposes JSON REST endpoints under the /api/v1 namespace.

docs.title: Get Challenge Listing
docs.text:
• Path: GET /api/v1/challenges
  • Authentication: Required
  • Returns: Array of active challenges.
[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "legacy_id": "ch_caesar",
    "title": "Caesar's Secret",
    "category": "Cryptography",
    "points": 50,
    "difficulty": "Easy"
  }
]

docs.title: Submit Flag Attempt
docs.text:
• Path: POST /api/v1/challenges/<id>/submit
  • Authentication: Required
  • Body: 
    { "flag": "FLAG{sample_flag}" }
  • Returns: Correct/incorrect status.

docs.title: Get Current Standings
docs.text:
• Path: GET /api/v1/scoreboard
  • Authentication: Optional
  • Returns: Leaderboard ranks and solved challenge timestamps.

docs.title: Competition Setup & Scoring
docs.text: Configure time-bounded events and select scoring algorithms that match your tournament style.

docs.title: 1. Event Scheduling
docs.text: In Admin → Competition, you can configure: - Start Time: When flag submission begins. - End Time: When scoring ends. - Is Active: Toggles platform accessibility. - Is Paused: Temp halts score updates. - Freeze Time: Restricts public scoreboard updates past this timestamp (allows organizers to build hype during final hours).

docs.title: 2. Point Allocation & Decay
docs.text: CTF Arena v2 supports three scoring modes:

docs.title: Static Points
docs.text: Challenges have a fixed value (e.g. 100 points) that never changes, regardless of when it is solved or by how many teams.

docs.title: Legacy Time Decay
docs.text: Points reduce gradually as time passes: - Decrements by 1 point per 10 seconds of competition elapsed. - Hard floor bounds at minimum_points configuration.

docs.title: Dynamic Decay
docs.text: Points decay as the number of solvers increases. Encourages finding unique exploits: - Points decrease dynamically with each successful solve on the challenge.

docs.title: Production Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide details best practices for running CTF Arena v2 in hostile production environments.

docs.title: 1. Stack Architecture
docs.text:
For staging and production, we recommend deploying behind a reverse proxy:

Competitor Client ──► HTTPS ──► Nginx Proxy ──► Gunicorn Web (Flask) ──► PostgreSQL DB

docs.title: 2. Hardening Environment Variables
docs.text:
Configure these settings in your .env file:

FLASK_ENV=production
SECRET_KEY=generate-a-strong-32-char-random-string
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@db-host:5432/ctfdb
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True
PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME=https
TRUSTED_PROXIES=1
ALLOWED_HOSTS=ctf.example.com

docs.title: 3. Gunicorn Execution
docs.text:
Start Gunicorn with threaded workers:

gunicorn wsgi:application \
  --bind 127.0.0.1:5000 \
  --workers 4 \
  --threads 2 \
  --timeout 60

docs.title: Native Docker Challenges
docs.text: CTF Arena v2 features native hosting of containerized exploits. Competitors can spawn individual, isolated instances of a challenge.

docs.title: 1. How It Works
docs.text:
Competitor Click "Start Instance"
            │
            ▼
  Web Application Calls Docker SDK
            │
            ▼
  Container Spawned ──► Dynamic Port Mapped ──► Connection String Displayed

Containers are bound to an expiry TTL (default 30 minutes). A background task prunes expired containers every 5 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Admin Configuration
docs.text:
1. Add Docker Image: Go to Admin → Docker → Images and register the image name (e.g. ctfarena/pwn-challenge:latest).
  2. Create Deployment Profile: Define CPU limits (e.g. 0.5 cores) and memory limits (e.g. 128m) to prevent resource exhaustion attacks.
  3. Link to Challenge: Associate the image and profile under the challenge editor settings.

docs.title: Local Installation & Setup
docs.text: Follow these steps to set up and run a CTF Arena development environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python: Version 3.10, 3.11, or 3.12.
  • Package Manager: pip.
  • Database: SQLite (built-in) or PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Installation Steps
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository: 

    git clone https://github.com/Sanjeyj/ctf-arena.git
cd ctf-arena

  2. Set up virtual environment: 

    python -m venv venv
# Windows
venv\Scripts\activate
# Linux / macOS
source venv/bin/activate

  3. Install python packages: 

    pip install -r requirements.txt

  4. Initialize database schema: 

    flask db upgrade
flask seed

  5. Start Flask web server: 

    export FLASK_ENV=development
flask run --port=5000

Open http://localhost:5000 in your web browser. Default admin login is admin / ctf_admin_2024.

docs.title: Security Controls & Hardening
docs.text: Review the security measures implemented in CTF Arena v2 and deployment recommendations.

docs.title: 1. Security Mitigations
docs.text:
• CSRF Enforcement: Handled via Flask-WTF. CSRF validation is active on all state-changing routes.
  • Session Cookie Flags: Hardened in production using HttpOnly=True, Secure=True, and SameSite=Lax.
  • Brute-Force & Lockouts: Limits consecutive failed login attempts to 5 per account. After threshold, accounts are locked and security events are logged.
  • File Upload Safeguards: Secure filename parsing prevents directory traversal exploit attempts. MIME-type validation rejects unapproved file extensions.

docs.title: 2. Recommended Hardening
docs.text:
1. SSL/TLS Configuration: Ensure Nginx reverse proxy forces TLS 1.2 or 1.3 with HSTS active.
  2. PostgreSQL Credentials: Run database services under dedicated read/write user roles with restricted permissions.
  3. Docker socket isolation: Restrict access to the Docker daemon Unix socket (/var/run/docker.sock).

docs.title: Teams Mode
docs.text: CTF Arena v2 supports optional Team-based competition modes.

docs.title: 1. Organizing Competitors
docs.text:
• Registration: Competitors register as normal.
  • Team Creation: Under the profile menu, any registered user can create a new team by assigning a unique name.
  • Joining a Team: Users enter the target team's join credentials to associate their profile.

docs.title: 2. Scoreboard Calculations
docs.text: When Team Mode is active: - Standings sum the scores of all users associated with the team. - Individual challenges solved by multiple members of the same team only award points to the team once (on the first solve timestamp). - Leaderboard ranks display team names instead of individual player usernames.
